SEC22A-01.note: Head is 'wild oat seeds'; the 'as well as' phrase does not join subjects, so plural active present 'germinate'. B tempts through the nearer singular 'bindweed'; A (passive) is grammatical in horticultural usage but 'Nobody sows or waters them... sprout on their own' rules out an agent.

SEC22A-02.note: 'A number of' takes a plural verb; present-tense follow-up ('emit', 'are') wants present perfect 'have adapted'. C attracts anyone who treats 'number' as the singular head.

SEC22A-03.note: 'Hydroponics' is singular despite the -s; the passage stays in present ('can cut', 'add'), so 'is practiced'. B tempts on the -s ending; C is the right number in the wrong tense.

SEC22A-04.convention: Both singular present forms are grammatical with a 'when' clause; the choice between simple and progressive is aspect/meaning, not a convention
SEC22A-04.note: Head 'a spheroid' is singular; the absolute phrase 'its outer cells wrapped...' is the plural attractor (A, C). I picked B because 'proliferates ... when the researchers add' reads as the drug CAUSING growth, contradicting 'its growth halts', while 'is proliferating when' frames growth already under way; but D is fully grammatical, so the item turns on semantics, not a convention.

SEC22A-05.note: Blank is the verb of the relative clause 'that the bird ___', whose subject is singular 'the bird' and which needs an active verb with 'that' as object; 'sprouted' is the main verb. Plural options C/B tempt via 'seeds'; passive A/C are ungrammatical with 'the bird' as subject. Past progressive is slightly unnatural (simple 'deposited' would be ideal) but it is the only legal option.

SEC22A-06.note: Head 'plasma units' is plural and the units are what is screened, so plural passive 'have been screened'. D attracts via the singular 'donor'/'antibody' just before the blank; C is plural but active (units doing the screening).

SEC22A-07.note: In 'the more X, the more Y' the object 'foraging bees' is fronted; the subject is 'a single plant', singular, and the parallel clause is simple present ('secrete'), so 'attracts'. C tempts because 'bees' precedes the verb; D is singular but breaks the present-tense parallel.

SEC22A-08.note: 'which' refers to plural 'samplers'; ongoing present context ('give', 'continue to draw') wants 'have been operating'. A is plural but past; B/D tempt via the singular 'county'.

SEC22B-01.note: Head 'piezometers' is plural; the relative clause holds singular 'technician'/'boat' as attractors; past narrative ('filled', 'opened') wants 'were recording'. B is right number, wrong tense.

SEC22B-02.note: Head 'wires' is plural; the 'by hydrogen' agent phrase requires passive, so 'are being attacked'. C tempts via the singular 'coating' in the interrupting clause (and 'cable', 'bridge'); D is plural but active, leaving 'by hydrogen' stranded.

SEC22B-03.note: Head 'A slab' singular despite plural 'trails' at the end of the long NP; the next sentence says the slab 'remains attached at its base', so the ongoing 'is detaching' not completed 'has detached'. B is the strong distractor and is ruled out only by the following sentence's meaning.

SEC22B-04.note: Head 'alignment' singular; 'between X and Y' supplies a compound-looking attractor. Past 'advanced'/'broke through' wants simple past 'was checked'; A is singular but present perfect clashes with the completed past frame.

SEC22B-05.note: 'nor' triggers subject-auxiliary inversion; the base form 'measure' later in the clause requires do-support, and the postposed subject 'the ... instrument' is singular, so 'does the'. 'has the ... measure' fails because 'has' would need 'measured'; C tempts via plural 'stations' in the first clause.

SEC22B-06.note: 'The latter' refers back to 'long wrought-iron rails' (plural; 'rolled in lengths' fits rails), and the narrative is past, so 'were costlier'. B is the strong trap because 'the latter' looks singular; a reader taking the antecedent as 'kind [of track]' could argue for B, a mild ambiguity worth a second look.

SEC22B-07.note: Head 'One such icy moon' singular; the parenthetical 'spacecraft measurements suggest' is the plural attractor. The delayed object 'towering jets' requires active, so 'has been ejecting'; D (passive) leaves the object stranded.

SEC22B-08.note: Head 'Attempts' plural; the paper already exists, so the stative present passive 'are documented'. C tempts via the singular 'astronomer'/'brightness'; D's progressive implies ongoing documenting, which clashes with a paper printed long ago.

SEC22C-01.note: Head 'questionnaire' singular (possessive 'statisticians'' is the attractor); 'from the season it was printed' marks a span up to now, which needs present perfect 'has been indispensable'. D is right number but simple present cannot take a 'from [past point]' span.

SEC22C-02.note: Compound predicate with plural subject 'Retired teachers' (singular attractors museum/diary/schoolmistress). Registries closed two winters ago, so the contribution is complete: 'have contributed', not ongoing 'have been contributing'. C is ruled out only by the following sentence.

SEC22C-03.note: In 'whose unsigned scripts ___' the subject is plural 'scripts'; the occupation narrative is past ('wrote', 'memorized'), so 'were being passed'. B tempts via 'playwright'; D is plural present.

SEC22C-04.note: 'which' refers to the varnish (or to the stripping as a whole); both readings are singular, and plural 'owners' is the attractor. The habitual 'Whenever...strips' frame wants simple present 'is logged'; A is singular but perfect aspect does not suit a habitual frame.

SEC22C-05.note: The 'that' clause could attach to 'the village priest' (singular) or 'The boys' (plural); context (the priest wears his everyday cassock, the boys are costumed by grandmothers) fixes it on the boys and on passive, so 'are dressed'. C, a priest-attached reading, is grammatical and ruled out only by the later sentence; D's active 'dressing' clashes with the grandmothers fitting the costumes.

SEC22C-06.note: Head 'script' singular; the 'unlike those of ... dramas' phrase is the plural attractor. 'in each of the seasons that followed its premiere' plus present 'write' marks a span up to now, so 'has been traveling'; B is singular but cannot carry the span.

SEC22C-07.convention: Agentless passive 'was being circulated' is standard; the choice between it and intransitive 'was circulating' is meaning, not a convention
SEC22C-07.note: Head 'The claim' singular (plural 'monks'/'charters' in the noun clause are the attractors), past frame. The intended cue is 'spread by itself... without any pamphlet', pointing to intransitive 'was circulating', but gossips passing it on are agents enough to defend the agentless passive A.

SEC22C-08.note: Inversion: the participial complement 'Complicating any attempt...' is fronted and the true subject 'faint ... initials' follows the verb, so plural; present frame ('disagree', 'read') wants 'are the'. B is strong because the gerund-like opening and singular 'panel'/'master' make a singular verb feel natural.

tells: Every item is the same 2x2 grid: number (singular/plural) crossed with one second axis (tense, voice, or aspect). Resolving only the second axis from the surrounding verbs halves every item without finding the subject, e.g. present-tense context kills two options in SEC22A-03, SEC22A-08, SEC22C-08, and past context in SEC22B-01, SEC22B-04, SEC22C-03.

In no item is the key decided by the noun right before the blank, and the attractor is always a noun of the opposite number to the head. A test-taker who learns 'skip the nearest noun, agree with the first noun of the sentence or clause' gets nearly every item (it fails only on SEC22A-05, SEC22B-05, SEC22C-05 and SEC22C-08, where the subject is not the first noun).

Six items settle the second axis by meaning from a later sentence rather than by a convention: SEC22A-01 (active, 'sprout on their own'), SEC22A-04 (progressive), SEC22B-03 ('remains attached'), SEC22C-02 (registries closed), SEC22C-05 (who is costumed), SEC22C-07 ('spread by itself'). A reader who learns that the later sentence always holds a cue can scan for it. Two of these (SEC22A-04, SEC22C-07) leave a second grammatical option standing.
No letter or option-wording tell: keys are spread evenly (A6, B6, C6, D6) and the key is not systematically the shortest or plainest option.
near_duplicates: singular head with a plural interrupting absolute or parenthetical phrase
relative clause 'that the X' whose own subject differs in number from the head
inverted order with the subject placed after the verb
plural head plus passive voice with singular attractor nouns before the blank
aspect or voice settled by meaning in the following sentence
singular head plus a 'from/in each of the seasons' span requiring present perfect
plural verb inside a nonrestrictive 'which/whose' clause
plural noun misleads before the verb, but agreement is with a different, number-fixed element
